messages:
Alex (AE): hey team — customer X is asking for a formal capacity plan for a 12-month enterprise commit. they expect 200 rps peak (chat) with median seq len ~256, occasional spikes to 800 rps for 30m. we need reserved sizing + autoscale / fallback plan. docs link?
Maria (SE): thanks Alex. couple quick qs: 1) priority for p99 latency (<=150ms?) 2) will they accept quantized model variant for burst? 3) region preference (us-east / eu-west)?
Alex (AE): p99 target is 200ms global. they want eu + us. they prefer identical output, but ok with slight quantization if quality checks pass.
Jeff (SalesOps): pricing note: reserved capacity discount tiers at 6/12/24 mo — also burst credits are billed separate. if we recommend N GPUs, we should show monthly committed cost vs on-demand blended. happy to calc once sizing is proposed.
Maria (SE): rough calc: for chat model (7B optimized) we get ~500 tokens/s per A100-80GB in steady-state batching at seq 256. with 200 rps and avg 100 tokens per response => 20k tokens/s total => ~40 tokens/s per request? wait doing quick math.
Maria (SE): concrete: 200 rps * 100 tokens = 20k tokens/s. If one GPU does 5k token/s (safe), need 4 GPUs reserved to cover base 200 rps with headroom. for bursts to 800 rps we need ~16 GPUs if we relied purely on reserved. propose reserved pool 6 GPUs + autoscale burst to 18 with prewarm slots and burst credits.
Sam (SRE): propose autoscale policy: keep reserved=6, prewarm=4 (keep warmed containers for fast spin-up), max=18, scale step=2, cooldown=30s. fallback rule: on capacity shortage route to a cheaper quantized variant or smaller model in same family.
Sam (SRE): sample autoscale config:

```
policy:
  reserved: 6
  prewarm: 4
  max: 18
  step: 2
  cooldown: 30s
fallbacks:
  - model: redwood-7b-quant
    max_latency_ms: 300
    routing: degrade-to-quant
```

Maria (SE): also recommend prefix/KV cache sizing: allocate ~40GB KV cache per GPU for 256-seq patterns. that'll reduce re-tokenization and lower token throughput by ~20% in ops.
Nina (CS): flag: customer requires private deployment with KMS + audit logs for commit. Dedicated private plan ok, but add note: private control plane adds ~2-3 week rollout and separate pricing. also security questionnaire will ask for isolation matrix.
Jeff (SalesOps): good call. i'll prepare a cost worksheet: committed 6 GPU baseline (monthly cost X), autoscale add-on pricing for burst, and one-time private deployment fee. need Maria/Sam numbers to finalize.
Alex (AE): can someone draft a one-pager on the recommended runway (capacity + fallback + SLA notes) by EOD? we'll attach to RFP.
Maria (SE): drafting now — will include performance caveats: p99 may slip to ~300ms during quantized fallback, but overall availability will stay. will link perf bench.
Sam (SRE): deploy-bot scheduled a prewarm job to simulate burst with 18 concurrent workers at 15:05 UTC. results will be posted here.
deploy-bot: prewarm job started: job_id=prewarm-1945, target=18 gpus, sim_rps=800, report ~15min after completion.
Nina (CS): also add runbook snippet for failover to region eu-west-1 if us-east saturated. include contact points for infra access.
Maria (SE): quick note: if they require strict token-level billing reconciliation, we'll need to enable per-request tracing (small perf hit). call that out.
Jeff (SalesOps): 👍 will prepare two pricing scenarios (6 reserved + burst vs 10 reserved minimal).
Alex (AE): perfect. once Maria posts the one-pager and Sam uploads prewarm results we can finalize for the customer. thanks all :thumbsup:
Sam (SRE): prewarm job complete — basic metrics: tail q99 latency ~220ms at 800rps with quantized fallback for 30% of requests. attaching summary: link to internal bench report: https://redwood.internal/bench/prewarm-1945
Maria (SE): got the report, i'll fold numbers into the doc and add recommended monitoring alerts (p99>220ms, queue>50ms).
Alex (AE): great — let's aim to send the plan to customer tomorrow morning.
Nina (CS): adding security questionnaire owner: @Nina (CS). i'll start the isolation matrix template and ping legal for addendum.
Jeff (SalesOps): i'll update pricing sheet and share.
Alex (AE): end of thread for now.
